about: GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC against bnlearn 5.2.1 on the papers' networks and on linear-Gaussian graphs, every node a target; the release summary's GS, Fast-IAMB, and HITON-PC entries are built from it
build: Andrey pre-release builds of the 0.18.0 release branch: 12 November 2026 for fast_iamb and hiton_pc as merged, 13 November 2026 for gs, whose shrink starts again from the first member after each removal
hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; Andrey and bnlearn ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes, except GS: its Andrey fits ran after bnlearn's, in separate runs on shared nodes of the same CPU model, so GS's times are indicative
verdict_rule: per cell (network or Gaussian graph, rows; 20 datasets, every node a target): per dataset, the mean over the targets with a nonempty true set of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1) (an empty answer counts precision 1, distance 1) and of the set's F1; D = Andrey's minus bnlearn's per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies wholly on the worse side of 0 (10,000 resamples of the datasets, default_rng(0)), better when wholly on the better side, a tie otherwise. A cell worse on seeds 0-19 on either measure was rerun on seeds 20-39 and is worse only when the fresh seeds agree; a cell better on seeds 0-19 was not rerun
error_metric: set_distance: the mean over the targets of the distance of the set's precision and recall from (1, 1); set_f1_loss: 1 minus the mean over the targets of the set's F1. The floor uses the set's errors, missing plus extra members (the wrong answers of andrey.metrics.target_answer_scores), against the empty set's, the true set's size
fit_protocol: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, every node of a dataset a target in one fit, no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored
seeds_note: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19; a rerun holds 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39
cells_note: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of the bnlearn repository network, columns that hold one value left out of every fit, each answering the empty set at its target, every set scored against the whole network; gauss:<d>:<rows>[:<mean degree>]: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graph, standardized, mean degree 2 unless given
comparisons_note: judged: the method against its bnlearn counterpart with the matching test; the others are context, reported and never judged: bnlearn with its plain test (mi, nominal degrees of freedom, no sparse-table rule), iamb and inter_iamb (Fast-IAMB's claim), mmpc, hiton_pc at its default max_depth 3, and hiton_pc without its rows-per-cell rule (an unshipped arm)
